china/modern-china.bfce236fc29b: New Culture Movement. From nineteen fifteen. A movement that liberated people’s thinking. Nineteen fifteen: Chen Duxiu, 陈独秀, founded Youth Magazine in Shanghai, renamed New Youth, 新青年, from Volume two, launching the movement. Leaders: Chen Duxiu, Li Dazhao, Lu Xun, Hu Shi and others; Peking University became one of its centres. Content: promote democracy, oppose autocracy; promote science, oppose ignorance; promote new morality, oppose old morality; promote new literature, oppose old literature. Hu Shi wrote “Suggestions for the Reform of Literature”; Lu Xun published the first vernacular short story, “A Madman’s Diary”. Later, Li Dazhao and others spread Marxism; the movement freed people’s minds and prepared the ground for Marxism in China.
china/modern-china.a12cd7e18d6d: Yuanmingyuan. Today: Haidian, Beijing. A vast Qing imperial garden, once called the “Garden of Gardens”. In eighteen sixty British and French troops looted it and set it on fire; today its ruins remind people never to forget.
china/modern-china.4b8a50af2c38: Nineteen eleven to nineteen twelve, The nineteen eleven Revolution. On October tenth, nineteen eleven, the Wuchang Uprising broke out. On January first, nineteen twelve, Sun Yat-sen became Provisional President in Nanjing — the Republic of China was born and the monarchy ended.
china/modern-china.0d7975467c54: Nineteen fifteen, The New Culture Movement. Chen Duxiu founded Youth Magazine, later New Youth, in Shanghai; the movement centred on Peking University. Its banners: democracy and science. Learning now reached the level of ideas.
china/modern-china.6ad7f5aa2212: Nineteen eleven Revolution. Nineteen eleven to nineteen twelve. Overthrew the autocratic monarchy. Sun Yat-sen, 孙中山, founded the Revive China Society, eighteen ninety-four, and the Tongmenghui, 同盟会, the “Revolutionary Alliance”, in Tokyo, nineteen oh five, whose programme — expel the Manchu rulers, restore China, found a republic, equalise land rights — became the Three Principles of the People, nationalism, democracy, people’s livelihood. October tenth, nineteen eleven: the Wuchang Uprising broke out and province after province responded. January first, nineteen twelve: Sun Yat-sen took office in Nanjing as Provisional President — the Republic of China was founded. The Qing emperor abdicated in February. March nineteen twelve: the Provisional Constitution of the Republic of China — the first law in Chinese history with the nature of a bourgeois-republican constitution. Significance: it ended more than two thousand years of autocratic monarchy and spread the idea of a democratic republic — but Yuan Shikai seized the fruits of the revolution.
china/modern-china.3e16fd1b2660: Taiping Heavenly Kingdom. Eighteen fifty-one to eighteen sixty-four. The peak of China’s old-style peasant wars. Eighteen fifty-one: Hong Xiuquan, 洪秀全, launched the Jintian Uprising in Guiping, Guangxi, and founded the “Taiping Heavenly Kingdom”, 太平天国, “Heavenly Kingdom of Great Peace”. Eighteen fifty-three: the Taiping army took Nanjing, renamed it Tianjing, 天京, “Heavenly Capital”, and made it the capital; it issued the Heavenly Land System, a plan to share out farmland equally. Eighteen fifty-nine: Hong Rengan put forward A New Work for Aid in Administration, the first fairly systematic plan in modern China for developing capitalism. After the Tianjing Incident, eighteen fifty-six, it declined; Tianjing fell in eighteen sixty-four and the movement failed. Significance: it dealt heavy blows to Qing rule and to foreign aggressors.
china/modern-china.76ba00836a83: Eighteen fifty-one to eighteen sixty-four, The Taiping Heavenly Kingdom. Hong Xiuquan rose at Jintian, Guangxi, eighteen fifty-one. The Taipings fought north and in eighteen fifty-three made Nanjing their capital, Tianjing. Crushed by Chinese and foreign forces, it fell in eighteen sixty-four.
china/modern-china.5e624b5138ae: Eighteen fifty-six to eighteen sixty, The Second Opium War. The Treaty of Tianjin opened ten more ports, deep up the Yangtze; the Convention of Peking added Tianjin and ceded Kowloon. Anglo-French troops burned the Old Summer Palace.
china/modern-china.12b989025cc3: Common mix-up: The Treaty of Nanjing ceded Hong Kong Island; the Kowloon area was ceded to Britain by the Convention of Peking. Nanjing’s indemnity was twenty-one million silver dollars, while Shimonoseki and the Boxer Protocol counted in taels of silver.
china/modern-china.6b20de9cf051: Second Opium War. Eighteen fifty-six to eighteen sixty. Anglo-French forces burned the Old Summer Palace. Supported by Russia and the USA, Britain and France launched the Second Opium War to open China’s market further. Eighteen fifty-eight Treaty of Tianjin: foreign envoys to live in Beijing; ten more ports including Hankou and Nanjing; foreign merchant ships and warships free to sail the Yangtze ports. Eighteen sixty: the Anglo-French army took Beijing, looted and burned the Old Summer Palace, 圆明园, the emperors’ garden palace. Convention of Peking: Tianjin opened as a port; the Kowloon area ceded to Britain. Taking advantage of the war, Tsarist Russia seized more than one point five million square kilometers of Chinese territory in the northeast and northwest. Impact: China’s semi-colonial status deepened further.
china/modern-china.5a1f2eec207e: Eighteen forty-two, Treaty of Nanjing, China’s first unequal treaty: cede Hong Kong Island, pay twenty-one million silver dollars, open five treaty ports — Guangzhou, Xiamen, Fuzhou, Ningbo, Shanghai — and accept “agreed tariffs”.
china/modern-china.1e3f2157e660: Peking University. Today: Beijing, the “Red Building” at Shatan; the university moved to Haidian in nineteen fifty-two. The Imperial University was the one reform of eighteen ninety-eight that survived. Twenty years later, as Peking University, it was a centre of the New Culture and May Fourth Movements.
china/modern-china.7fce918bec3e: Self-Strengthening Movement. Eighteen sixties to eighteen nineties. Learning Western technology: “self-strengthening”, 自强, and “seeking wealth”, 求富. Leaders: Prince Gong, Yixin, at court; Zeng Guofan, Li Hongzhang, Zuo Zongtang and Zhang Zhidong in the provinces. Guiding idea: “Chinese learning as the foundation, Western learning for practical use.” Early stage, slogan “self-strengthening”: military industries such as the Anqing Arsenal, the Jiangnan Arsenal and the Fuzhou Navy Yard. Later stage, slogan “seeking wealth”: civilian industries such as the China Merchants Steam Navigation Company and the Hanyang Iron Works; also new navies such as the Beiyang Fleet, new-style schools and students sent abroad. The Beiyang Fleet’s total defeat in the Sino-Japanese War marked its failure, but it brought in Western technology and China’s first modern enterprises — it is seen as the start of China’s modernisation.
china/modern-china.de9493f626df: Hundred Days’ Reform. Eighteen ninety-eight. Reformists tried to build a constitutional monarchy. Eighteen ninety-five: Kang Youwei and the provincial graduates in Beijing for the exam petitioned the emperor — the “Gongche Petition”, 公车上书. June eleventh, eighteen ninety-eight: Emperor Guangxu issued the edict “Defining the State Policy” and launched the reform. Measures: reform government offices and appoint reformers; encourage private mines and factories; open new schools, drop the “eight-legged essay”, a rigid essay form used in the old exams, found the Imperial University of Peking; train a new army and navy. September twenty-first: Empress Dowager Cixi staged a coup and the reform failed; Tan Sitong and the other “Six Gentlemen” were killed. It lasted one hundred three days. Significance: a patriotic political movement and an ideological enlightenment.
china/modern-china.97f3b416f9da: Eighteen forty, The Opium War. In June eighteen thirty-nine Lin Zexu destroyed confiscated opium at Humen. In eighteen forty Britain used this as an excuse to launch the Opium War — the beginning of China’s modern history.
china/modern-china.75a50b505bbc: Watch out: Modern history begins with the outbreak of the war in eighteen forty, not with the eighteen forty-two treaty. The Treaty of Nanjing was the first unequal treaty in modern Chinese history.
china/modern-china.b3ded45bec3b: Sino-Japanese War and Treaty of Shimonoseki. Eighteen ninety-four to eighteen ninety-five. Greatly deepened China’s semi-colonial status. Eighteen ninety-four: Japan provoked the war. In the Battle of the Yellow Sea, Deng Shichang, 邓世昌, captain of the warship Zhiyuan, died a hero. Early eighteen ninety-five: the Beiyang Fleet was completely destroyed at Weihaiwei. April eighteen ninety-five Treaty of Shimonoseki: cede the Liaodong Peninsula, Taiwan with all its affiliated islands, and the Penghu Islands to Japan; pay two hundred million taels of silver; open Shashi, Chongqing, Suzhou and Hangzhou; allow Japan to open factories in treaty ports. Under pressure from Russia, Germany and France, Japan returned the Liaodong Peninsula, but China paid thirty million taels to “redeem” it. After the war the powers began a scramble to carve up China.
china/modern-china.bc80650756e1: Memory rhyme: Jintian, eighteen fifty-one, capital at Tianjing, eighteen fifty-three, Tianjing falls, eighteen sixty-four.

china/natural-wonders.f44fd72f803e: Dunhuang Yardang, Gansu. Gansu, old lake-bed layers, wind-carved ridges. Long ridges shaped like upside-down boats or a fleet of ships, all pointing the same way — the way the wind blows. Yardang comes from a Uyghur word for a steep ridge. Locals call such places “devil city”, 魔鬼城, because the wind howls through them. The rock is layers of mud and sand from an old lake. Wind-blown sand works like a sandblaster on the softer layers. Dry lake, strong wind and sand equals yardang.
china/natural-wonders.80c6c6201151: Zhangye Danxia, Gansu. Gansu, red sandstone and mudstone, Danxia, red beds. Hills striped red, orange, yellow and white — the “rainbow mountains”. Danxia, 丹霞, means “rosy clouds”. The landform is named after Danxia Mountain in Guangdong, where red cliffs were first described. The colours come from minerals, mostly iron: rusty iron oxide is red, other minerals are yellow, white or grey-green. Red beds, uplift and erosion equals Danxia.
china/natural-wonders.52b7e8a1e50c: Stone Forest, Shilin, Yunnan. Yunnan, limestone, karst stone forest. A “forest” of grey limestone blades and pinnacles, packed so tightly that paths squeeze between them like a maze. Some pinnacles are taller than a seven-storey building. Same rock as Guilin, but here the water cut mostly along close-set vertical cracks, so you get blades instead of big towers. Close cracks, a crowd of stone blades.
china/natural-wonders.ff2a4d6cc6e4: Mount Huangshan, Anhui. Anhui, granite, peaks and odd rocks. Famous for its “four wonders”: odd-shaped pines, strange rocks, a sea of clouds and hot springs. The highest peak, Lotus Peak, is about one thousand eight hundred sixty-five meters, six thousand one hundred feet. Granite starts as magma that cools slowly deep underground — the slow cooling grows big crystals you can see. Cracks, joints, cut the granite into blocks; weathering along them makes the sharp peaks and balanced boulders. Cooled underground, lifted up, carved along cracks.
china/natural-wonders.be235c09ce9d: Zhangjiajie, Wulingyuan, Hunan. Hunan, quartz sandstone, peak forest. More than three thousand sandstone pillars, many over two hundred meters, six hundred fifty feet, tall — like a forest of sixty-storey skyscrapers with pine trees on the roof. The rock is quartz sandstone, which water can’t dissolve. Instead, flowing water, frost and gravity pried it apart along vertical cracks. One pillar was renamed “Avatar Hallelujah Mountain” after the film’s floating mountains. Sandstone, uplift, cracks and water equals pillars.
china/natural-wonders.28f769fd4cf3: Guilin landscapes, Li River. Guangxi, limestone, karst peak forest. Hundreds of steep limestone towers rise straight out of flat rice fields, with the Li River, 漓江, winding between them. Inside, the hills are full of caves such as Reed Flute Cave, 芦笛岩 — water has been eating the rock from within, too. The scene is printed on the back of China’s twenty-yuan banknote. Limestone, rain and time equals towers and caves.
china/natural-wonders.01d14aa28f0b: Jiuzhaigou and Huanglong, Sichuan. Sichuan, travertine, calcium carbonate, lakes and pools. Clear turquoise lakes and thousands of terraced pools, rimmed by creamy rock dams. The dams are travertine, 钙华: calcium carbonate dropped by water — the same stuff as the white crust in a kettle. In August twenty seventeen an earthquake in Jiuzhaigou broke the dam of Sparkling Lake, 火花海, and damaged Nuorilang Falls; both were repaired and the park reopened. Dissolve underground, drop it at the surface.
china/natural-wonders.6a935caa2e03: Qomolangma, Mount Everest. Xizang, Tibet, China-Nepal border, eight thousand eight hundred forty-eight point eight six meters. The world’s highest peak: eight thousand eight hundred forty-eight point eight six meters, twenty-nine thousand thirty-two feet, measured jointly by China and Nepal in twenty twenty. That’s about twenty Empire State Buildings stacked up. The rock near the summit is limestone with fossils of sea creatures — it was once the floor of an ocean. The Indian Plate is still pushing north into the Eurasian Plate, so the Himalayas are still rising by a few millimetres a year. Plates collide, sea floor climbs to the sky.

china/new-era.62eff9742183: Don’t mix up: The basic station has three modules, one core and two labs — not counting visiting spacecraft.
china/new-era.1c044d109aef: Twenty twenty-three. A home-built airliner carries passengers. On May twenty-eighth, twenty twenty-three, the C nine one nine — a passenger jet designed and built in China, about the size of a Boeing seven three seven — flew its first commercial flight, from Shanghai to Beijing.
china/new-era.da4657b1783a: Robotic arm. A ten-metre helping hand outside the station. About ten meters long, with seven joints — like a human arm with a shoulder, elbow and wrist. It can “crawl” along the outside of the station, end over end. It moves astronauts during spacewalks and can shift heavy equipment.
china/new-era.d2cec7337b92: Twenty forty-nine. Second centenary goal. By the middle of the century — the hundredth birthday of the People’s Republic in twenty forty-nine — build China into a great modern socialist country that is prosperous, strong, democratic, culturally advanced, harmonious and beautiful.
china/new-era.1072021cbad1: Twenty seventeen. The nineteenth National Congress: a “new era”. In October twenty seventeen the nineteenth National Congress declared that socialism with Chinese characteristics had entered a new era. The country’s main challenge had changed: people now wanted a better life, but development was still unbalanced and inadequate.
china/new-era.c78107d2e353: Tianhe core module. 天和, “Harmony of the Heavens” — the control centre and main living room. The first piece in orbit. About sixteen point six meters long — roughly a city bus and a half. It steers the whole station and holds the sleeping quarters, kitchen and exercise bike. Its round “node” at the front has ports where other modules and spacecraft dock.
china/new-era.59e3b8183a7e: Twenty nineteen. First landing on the Moon’s far side. On January third, twenty nineteen, the Chang’e four probe, 嫦娥 is the Moon goddess of Chinese legend, made the first soft landing in history on the far side of the Moon — the side we never see from Earth. On October first the People’s Republic of China turned seventy.
china/new-era.f811fae6c1d2: Tianzhou cargo spacecraft. 天舟, “Heavenly Vessel” — the delivery truck. No crew on board: it flies and docks automatically. It brings food, water, experiments and rocket fuel — several tonnes at a time. When its job is done it is filled with trash and burns up in the atmosphere.
china/new-era.b474c8fa8c39: Don’t mix up: Shenzhou five, two thousand three, was the first crewed flight; it did not go to a space station.
china/new-era.1e2af7179005: Twenty twenty-four. Samples from the Moon’s far side. In June twenty twenty-four Chang’e six brought back the first samples ever collected from the far side of the Moon. On October first the People’s Republic of China turned seventy-five.
china/new-era.d15a1ef3b7c8: Twenty eighteen. Written into the Constitution. In March twenty eighteen China’s national legislature, the National People’s Congress, amended the Constitution. Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era was written into it. Twenty eighteen was also the fortieth anniversary of “reform and opening up”.
china/new-era.5b1c0134de42: Twenty fifteen. Five ideas for how to grow. In October twenty fifteen the CPC put forward a new development philosophy, 新发展理念, in five words: innovation, coordination, green, openness and sharing. Growth should be smarter, more balanced, cleaner, more connected to the world, and fairer.
china/new-era.2c625fcf3186: Twenty sixteen. “China’s Sky Eye” opens. In September twenty sixteen FAST — a radio telescope five hundred metres wide, as big as about thirty soccer fields — began listening to the universe from a natural bowl in the hills of Guizhou Province. Its nickname is “China’s Sky Eye”, 中国天眼.
china/new-era.b99f7bea535d: Wentian lab module. 问天, “Quest for the Heavens” — a science lab and backup control room. Mostly life-science experiments: how plants, cells and small animals do in weightlessness. It has extra sleeping cabins, so six astronauts can be aboard during a crew handover. It also has its own airlock for spacewalks.
china/new-era.2b120dd72b19: Solar wings. Turn sunlight into electricity. The big wings on the lab modules are about twenty-seven meters long each when unrolled. They are flexible, thin as paper, and turn to follow the Sun. The station circles Earth about every ninety minutes, so batteries take over in Earth’s shadow.
china/new-era.4a5841bce5a0: Don’t mix up: Three sets of words are easy to confuse. The “Five-sphere Integrated Plan”, 五位一体, is the overall layout: economy, politics, culture, society and the environment. The “Four Comprehensives”, 四个全面, are the strategy. “Innovation, coordination, green, openness, sharing” is the new development philosophy, 新发展理念.
china/new-era.7c82c981a0ac: Twenty fourteen. The “Four Comprehensives” strategy. In twenty fourteen the leadership put forward a four-part strategy called the “Four Comprehensives”, 四个全面. “Comprehensive” means “in every respect”.
china/new-era.dd183c2e860c: Twenty twenty. A hard year with big finishes. In twenty twenty China fought the COVID nineteen epidemic. By November the last poor counties had been lifted out of poverty. The BeiDou three satellite navigation system — China’s own GPS — went global, and China’s economy passed one hundred trillion yuan for the first time.
china/new-era.db576cf1c764: Twenty twenty-two. The twentieth National Congress: Chinese modernisation. In October twenty twenty-two the twentieth National Congress set the central task for the years ahead: build a great modern socialist country and advance national rejuvenation through a Chinese path to modernisation, 中国式现代化. That year the Tiangong space station was completed.
china/new-era.0a1df5ce1812: Shenzhou crewed spacecraft. 神舟, “Divine Vessel” — the astronauts’ ride up and down. It carries three astronauts. Shenzhou twelve took the first crew to Tiangong in June twenty twenty-one. In two thousand three Shenzhou five carried Yang Liwei, making China the third country to send a person into space on its own. Crews now stay about six months, then hand over to the next crew in orbit.
china/new-era.b522a09c0483: Twenty twelve. The eighteenth National Congress and the “Chinese Dream”. In November twenty twelve the Communist Party of China, CPC, held its eighteenth National Congress — a meeting held every five years that sets the country’s direction. Xi Jinping, 习近平, became General Secretary. Days later he named a goal: the “Chinese Dream”, 中国梦.
china/new-era.230b2d271918: Twenty thirteen. “Targeted” help for poor villages. In November twenty thirteen, visiting Shibadong, 十八洞, a mountain village in Hunan Province, Xi Jinping put forward “targeted poverty alleviation”, 精准扶贫: find out exactly who is poor and why, then help household by household.
china/new-era.4dfa05ef89c8: Twenty thirty-five. Goal for twenty thirty-five. Step one of the plan set by the nineteenth and twentieth Congresses: by twenty thirty-five, basically achieve socialist modernisation.
china/new-era.511864776fdd: Mengtian lab module. 梦天, “Dreaming of the Heavens” — the last big piece. Mostly physics experiments in microgravity, including very precise atomic clocks. When it docked, the station reached its T shape — three modules, about sixty-six tonnes. That is about one-sixth the mass of the ISS, which was built by fifteen countries.
china/new-era.e0305ffb42c2: Taizicheng. Today: Chongli, Zhangjiakou, Hebei. A station in the snowy hills of Chongli, where skiing events of the twenty twenty-two Winter Olympics were held. Trains from Beijing take about an hour.
china/new-era.b259f4fcf0ee: Don't mix up: Wentian arrived before Mengtian — July, then October twenty twenty-two.
china/new-era.488c47fe7524: Twenty twenty-one. First centenary goal reached. On July first, twenty twenty-one, the CPC’s one hundredth birthday, Xi Jinping announced that China had built a “moderately prosperous society in all respects”, 全面建成小康社会; xiǎokāng means “fairly well-off”. In February China had declared complete victory in the fight against poverty.

china/population-resources.4ccc7ddc661e: Inner Mongolia. Short name: 内蒙古, about twenty-four point one million people. Area: about one million one hundred eighty-three thousand square kilometers. Density: about twenty people per square kilometer, rank thirty-one of thirty-four. The Heihe-Tengchong Line runs through this province. Sparser than the national average, about one hundred forty-seven people per square kilometer.
china/population-resources.48474d77d77f: Gansu. Short name: 甘 or 陇, about twenty-five point zero million people. Area: about four hundred twenty-five thousand eight hundred square kilometers. Density: about fifty-nine people per square kilometer, rank thirty of thirty-four. The Heihe-Tengchong Line runs through this province. Sparser than the national average, about one hundred forty-seven people per square kilometer.
china/population-resources.f443d079a194: Shanxi. Short name: 晋, about thirty-four point nine million people. Area: about one hundred fifty-six thousand seven hundred square kilometers. Density: about two hundred twenty-three people per square kilometer, rank twenty-one of thirty-four. Lies southeast of the Heihe-Tengchong Line, the crowded side. Denser than the national average, about one hundred forty-seven people per square kilometer.
china/population-resources.1caf60de603a: Heilongjiang. Short name: 黑, about thirty-one point nine million people. Area: about four hundred seventy-three thousand square kilometers. Density: about sixty-seven people per square kilometer, rank twenty-nine of thirty-four. The Heihe-Tengchong Line runs through this province. Sparser than the national average, about one hundred forty-seven people per square kilometer.
china/population-resources.d4ae2dd875c1: A huge population. About one point four one billion people, twenty twenty census. China is one of the most populous countries in the world: about one point four one billion people in the thirty-one provinces, regions and municipalities, twenty twenty. Average density is about one hundred forty-seven people per square kilometer, but it differs hugely from place to place. Growth has slowed. New challenges include an ageing population; birth policies keep being improved, for example the three-child policy, twenty twenty-one. Many people, a big base: dense in the southeast, sparse in the northwest.
china/population-resources.30208e8710a7: Xinjiang. Short name: 新, about twenty-five point nine million people. Area: about one million six hundred sixty-four thousand nine hundred square kilometers. Density: about sixteen people per square kilometer, rank thirty-two of thirty-four. Lies northwest of the Heihe-Tengchong Line, the sparse side. Sparser than the national average, about one hundred forty-seven people per square kilometer.
china/population-resources.8a2f1600f575: Jilin. Short name: 吉, about twenty-four point one million people. Area: about one hundred eighty-seven thousand four hundred square kilometers. Density: about one hundred twenty-eight people per square kilometer, rank twenty-six of thirty-four. Lies southeast of the Heihe-Tengchong Line, the crowded side. Sparser than the national average, about one hundred forty-seven people per square kilometer.
china/population-resources.7d1f2405a373: Heihe-Tengchong Line. Dense southeast, sparse northwest. Proposed by geographer Hu Huanyong in nineteen thirty-five, so it is also called the Hu Line. Southeast of the line: about forty-three percent of the land but about ninety-four percent of the people. Northwest: about fifty-seven percent of the land, only about six percent of the people, approximately. The southeast is lower and flatter, with a wetter climate, a long history of farming, good transport and a strong economy. The northwest has plateaus, mountains and deserts, and is dry or very cold. Draw a line from Heihe to Tengchong: crowded southeast, empty northwest.

china/prc-founding.25f05bc03d5a: Steel truss. Triangles make a frame strong but light. Nine spans, each about one hundred twenty-eight meters long — longer than a football field. The whole bridge is about one thousand six hundred seventy meters long: a little more than one mile.
china/prc-founding.47f39576486c: The “Cultural Revolution”: ten years of turmoil. Nineteen sixty-six to nineteen seventy-six. In the mid-nineteen sixties Mao Zedong wrongly believed the Party and country faced a danger of capitalism returning, and in nineteen sixty-six launched the “Cultural Revolution”. Two cliques — led by Lin Biao, 林彪, and by Jiang Qing, 江青 — used the chaos to try to seize power. Democracy and law were trampled; many officials and ordinary people were persecuted, including President Liu Shaoqi, 刘少奇. Nineteen seventy-one: the Lin Biao clique was smashed. October nineteen seventy-six: the “Gang of Four” was smashed — the “Cultural Revolution” was over. The textbook’s judgement: it brought the Party, the country and the people the most severe setback and losses since nineteen forty-nine.
china/prc-founding.34e69e1e9633: Memory hook: September: plan it. October first: proclaim it.
china/prc-founding.f93929dba984: Memory hook: nineteen fifty-one — Tibet, peacefully; the mainland is one.
china/prc-founding.da867f7e7646: The first National People’s Congress and the Constitution. September nineteen fifty-four. September nineteen fifty-four: more than one thousand two hundred elected deputies met in Beijing for the first National People’s Congress, NPC. They adopted the Constitution of the People’s Republic of China — the country’s first socialist-type constitution. The system of people’s congresses became China’s fundamental political system, as it still is today.
china/prc-founding.e0fbb5cf4f4d: Changchun. In nineteen fifty-six the First Automobile Works in Changchun built New China’s first trucks, the “Jiefang”, Liberation.
china/prc-founding.e4224e23a582: Watch out: The Eighth Congress, nineteen fifty-six, set a correct course; the mistakes of nineteen fifty-eight came from leaving that course.
china/prc-founding.c05932f3a1f6: Memory hook: October nineteen fifty across the Yalu; July nineteen fifty-three the guns fall silent.
china/prc-founding.fbac9879a7ea: Watch out: Two different bodies: the consultative conference, CPPCC, nineteen forty-nine, advises; the National People’s Congress, from nineteen fifty-four, makes the laws.
china/prc-founding.768ebc2f818b: The People’s Republic is founded. October first, nineteen forty-nine. September nineteen forty-nine: a big conference of many parties and groups, the CPPCC, met in Beiping. It passed the Common Programme, 共同纲领, which worked as a temporary constitution, and elected Mao Zedong, 毛泽东, Chairman. It chose the five-star red flag, the song “March of the Volunteers” as the anthem, and renamed Beiping “Beijing” — the capital. October first, nineteen forty-nine: at Tian’anmen, 天安门, “Gate of Heavenly Peace”, Mao announced the new government to a crowd of three hundred thousand. Why it matters: a new era in Chinese history — the Chinese people “stood up” and became masters of their own country.
china/prc-founding.02492f1aa360: Daqing Oilfield. Today: Daqing, Heilongjiang. Workers led by “Iron Man” Wang Jinxi drilled for oil here in freezing cold. By nineteen sixty-three China could supply almost all its own oil.
china/prc-founding.816463147081: Peaceful liberation of Tibet. Nineteen fifty-one. Nineteen fifty-one: the central government and the local government of Tibet signed an agreement, and Tibet was liberated peacefully — without a war. Why it matters: the Chinese mainland was now unified, and China’s many ethnic groups were united. Nineteen fifty-four: two highways were finished across the “roof of the world” to Lhasa, 拉萨, Tibet’s main city.
china/prc-founding.19715980401a: Watch out: The socialist system dates from the end of nineteen fifty-six, transformations complete, not from nineteen forty-nine, founding.
china/prc-founding.5e66a16c0edc: Land reform. Nineteen fifty to nineteen fifty-two. Before: a small class of landlords owned much of the farmland; most peasants rented fields and paid heavy rents. Nineteen fifty: the Land Reform Law ended landlord ownership and gave the land to the peasants themselves. By the end of nineteen fifty-two it was basically complete: about three hundred million peasants — twice the whole US population then — received land. Why it matters: a feudal land system more than two thousand years old was destroyed; farm output rose and the ground was prepared for industrialisation.
china/prc-founding.d6a3247e71c0: “Great Leap Forward” and people’s communes: mistakes in the search. Nineteen fifty-eight to nineteen sixties. Nineteen fifty-eight: wanting to catch up fast, the Party launched the “Great Leap Forward”, impossibly high output targets, and merged co-operatives into giant people’s communes. The textbook’s judgement: this ignored objective economic laws. Sky-high targets, orders given blindly, exaggerated reports and a “communist wind” spread widely. Together with natural disasters, this led to serious economic hardship in nineteen fifty-nine to nineteen sixty-one — look at the dip in the harvest chart. From the winter of nineteen sixty the Party and government began to correct the mistakes and adjust the economy, which then recovered and grew.
china/prc-founding.95797309709d: The three great transformations. Nineteen fifty-three to nineteen fifty-six. Farming: peasant families were led to join agricultural producers’ co-operatives and farm together. Handicrafts: craft workers formed co-operatives too. Private factories and shops: became joint state-private businesses; the state bought out the owners step by step. By the end of nineteen fifty-six it was basically done: private ownership of the means of production had become public ownership. The basic socialist system was established. The textbook also notes faults: it was done too fast and in too uniform a way.
china/prc-founding.5856937f6696: Memory hook: nineteen fifty the law, nineteen fifty-two it’s done: the fields belong to the farmers.
china/prc-founding.9f9ec56d098d: Watch out: It ended in October nineteen seventy-six with the fall of the “Gang of Four” — not in nineteen seventy-one. The textbook does not treat it as a real revolution or as progress.
china/prc-founding.360f3e4719c5: Memory hook: sixty-four atom bomb, sixty-seven hydrogen bomb, seventy a satellite sings.
china/prc-founding.c8f2da0ac668: Anshan Steel. Today: Anshan, Liaoning. In nineteen fifty-three three big new works at Anshan started producing — the beginning of New China’s steel industry.
china/prc-founding.034176b689cf: Memory hook: Eighth Congress, nineteen fifty-six: develop production.
china/prc-founding.e07fd2ed153a: Memory hook: nineteen sixty-six begins, nineteen seventy-six ends: ten lost years.
china/prc-founding.8093880e4c45: Watch out: The conference, September, came before the ceremony, October first. The Common Programme was only a temporary constitution — the first real one came in nineteen fifty-four.
china/prc-founding.dbdef9efa003: Watch out: The plan put heavy industry first — not farming or light industry. And the Nanjing bridge, nineteen sixty-eight, is not a First Five-Year Plan project; the Wuhan bridge, nineteen fifty-seven, is.
china/prc-founding.4977ba92056f: War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea. Nineteen fifty to nineteen fifty-three. June nineteen fifty: civil war broke out in Korea. US-led “UN forces” entered the war and pushed north to the Yalu River, 鸭绿江, China’s border; the US Navy also sailed into the Taiwan Strait. October nineteen fifty: the Chinese People’s Volunteers, commanded by Peng Dehuai, 彭德怀, crossed the Yalu to fight beside the Korean army. Heroes every Chinese student knows: Huang Jiguang, 黄继光, and Qiu Shaoyun, 邱少云. The volunteers were called “the most beloved people”. July nineteen fifty-three: the armistice was signed. China had protected its security and won peaceful years to build its economy.
china/prc-founding.f62554ee2cf4: Watch out: The volunteers’ commander was Peng Dehuai. They entered Korea in October nineteen fifty — four months after the Korean civil war began in June.
china/prc-founding.60f92ce5e2b3: The Party’s Eighth National Congress. Nineteen fifty-six. Nineteen fifty-six: the Communist Party of China held its Eighth National Congress in Beijing. It judged that the main problem was now the gap between people’s need for a better economy and culture and the country’s backward state. So the main task was to concentrate on developing production — turning a backward farming country into an advanced industrial one as quickly as possible. The decade nineteen fifty-six to nineteen sixty-six is called “ten years of all-round socialist construction”.
china/prc-founding.b2ff592c8a01: Memory hook: fifty-four: first Congress, first Constitution.
china/prc-founding.4543955e69f8: Achievements and role models. Nineteen sixties to nineteen seventies. Oil: workers led by “Iron Man” Wang Jinxi, 王进喜, opened the Daqing, 大庆, oil field; by nineteen sixty-five China produced all the oil it needed. Defence and space: first atomic bomb, October nineteen sixty-four, guided nuclear missile, nineteen sixty-six, hydrogen bomb, nineteen sixty-seven, and the satellite Dongfanghong one, 东方红一号, “The East Is Red one”, April nineteen seventy — one year after Apollo eleven. Scientist Deng Jiaxian, 邓稼先, is honoured as a founder of the programme. Science: insulin made in the lab, nineteen sixty-five; Yuan Longping’s, 袁隆平, hybrid rice, nineteen seventy-three. Role models: Jiao Yulu, 焦裕禄, a county leader who worked himself to exhaustion for poor farmers in Lankao; Lei Feng, 雷锋, a young soldier famous for helping others. Villagers in Lin County, Henan, cut the Red Flag Canal, 红旗渠, through cliffs by hand to bring water home.
china/prc-founding.2faea0364333: Shenyang. Shenyang is a big industrial city. Its aircraft works built New China’s first jet fighter in nineteen fifty-six, and the Japanese invasion began here on September eighteenth, nineteen thirty-one.
china/prc-founding.bff5c8ddc1e2: Lower deck: the railway. A double-track railway runs underneath — a “double-decker” bridge. It linked the Beijing-Hankou and Guangzhou-Hankou lines into one north-south trunk line, like joining New York to Atlanta by rail for the first time. Before nineteen fifty-seven every train was cut into pieces and carried over on a ferry.
china/prc-founding.d9ae771d4832: Bridgehead towers. Towers about thirty-five meters tall stand at each end, with stairs and lifts from the riverbank up to the road. The bridge runs between Turtle Hill, 龟山, and Snake Hill, 蛇山.
china/prc-founding.e7d5bebad0b3: The First Five-Year Plan. Nineteen fifty-three to nineteen fifty-seven. Goal: put most effort into heavy industry, steel, machines, vehicles, to lay the first foundations of an industrial country with a modern defence. Nineteen fifty-three: Anshan Steel, 鞍钢, opened three huge projects. Nineteen fifty-six: the first Chinese-built truck rolled out in Changchun, the first jet plane was built, and the Shenyang machine-tool plant opened. Nineteen fifty-seven: the Wuhan Yangtze River Bridge joined north and south; three highways, Sichuan-Tibet, Qinghai-Tibet, Xinjiang-Tibet, climbed onto the Tibetan Plateau. Result: China began to change from a backward farming country toward socialist industrialisation. Most targets were beaten.

china/prc.d58fd4d0de10: Nineteen fifty-three to nineteen fifty-six, Industrialisation begins. The First Five-Year Plan put heavy industry first: Anshan Steel, the first Jiefang truck from Changchun, nineteen fifty-six, the first jet aircraft from Shenyang, nineteen fifty-six, the Wuhan Yangtze River Bridge, nineteen fifty-seven, and the Sichuan-Tibet and Qinghai-Tibet highways, nineteen fifty-four. In nineteen fifty-four the first Constitution was adopted; by nineteen fifty-six the socialist transformation was basically complete.
china/prc.7787432685c4: Watch out: The Qinghai-Tibet Railway, two thousand six, is a plateau railway, not a high-speed line.
china/prc.ae3d5a10f2b2: Watch out: Chang’e four landed on the far side of the Moon, which is never seen from Earth.
china/prc.e534c2988089: Nineteen ninety-seven, nineteen ninety-nine, Hong Kong and Macao return. Following Deng Xiaoping’s idea of “one country, two systems”, China resumed sovereignty over Hong Kong on July first, nineteen ninety-seven, and Macao on December twentieth, nineteen ninety-nine. Taiwan is an inalienable part of China; cross-Strait exchanges keep growing.
china/prc.e0fbb5cf4f4d: Changchun. In nineteen fifty-six the First Automobile Works in Changchun built New China’s first trucks, the “Jiefang”, Liberation.
china/prc.c75b9a220992: Tian’anmen. On October first, nineteen forty-nine, Chairman Mao Zedong stood on this gate tower and proclaimed the founding of the People’s Republic of China. The square in front can hold about a million people.
china/prc.8e6184cf0e20: Shenzhou five and the Long March rockets. Two thousand three. China’s first crewed spaceflight. October two thousand three: Shenzhou five, launched by a Long March two F rocket, carried Yang Liwei, China’s first astronaut, into space. China became the third country able to send people into space on its own. Two thousand eight: Shenzhou seven — Zhai Zhigang made China’s first spacewalk. The Long March rocket family carries China’s satellites, spaceships and space-station modules.
china/prc.02492f1aa360: Daqing Oilfield. Today: Daqing, Heilongjiang. Workers led by “Iron Man” Wang Jinxi drilled for oil here in freezing cold. By nineteen sixty-three China could supply almost all its own oil.
china/prc.a971c788e532: Summary. In seventy years New China stood up, nineteen forty-nine, began to grow prosperous through reform and opening up, nineteen seventy-eight, and in the new era is becoming strong. Now explore the three D hall of achievements!
china/prc.27d2119f63b5: BeiDou Navigation Satellite System. Twenty twenty. China’s own global navigation system. BeiDou is a global satellite navigation system built and operated independently by China. Twenty twenty: the BeiDou three global system was completed and opened for service. It is used in transport, farming, disaster relief and everyday phones.
china/prc.dd3b35662876: Tiangong space station. Twenty twenty-two. China’s own space station in orbit. The station has three modules: the Tianhe core module and the Wentian and Mengtian lab modules, forming a “T” shape. End of twenty twenty-two: the Tiangong space station was fully completed. Astronauts live and work on board in rotation and give “Tiangong classes” to students on Earth.
china/prc.3cbc4a9d9077: Memory rhyme: sixty-four atom bomb, sixty-seven hydrogen bomb, seventy satellite.
china/prc.a2f6b491024b: Nineteen fifty to nineteen fifty-three, Consolidating the new republic. In October nineteen fifty the Chinese People’s Volunteers, led by Peng Dehuai, crossed the Yalu River; the armistice was signed in July nineteen fifty-three. Tibet was peacefully liberated in nineteen fifty-one, and land reform abolished the feudal land system by the end of nineteen fifty-two.
china/prc.c2142a7d6381: Two thousand three to twenty twenty-two, Science and technology soar. Shenzhou five carried Yang Liwei into space, two thousand three; Chang’e reached the Moon, two thousand seven, and its far side, twenty nineteen; high-speed rail linked Beijing and Tianjin, two thousand eight; BeiDou went global, twenty twenty; the Tiangong space station was completed, twenty twenty-two.
china/prc.9cd9d47267c7: Nineteen fifty-six to nineteen seventy-six, Construction in hard times. Despite setbacks, there were great achievements: the Daqing oil field, “Iron Man” Wang Jinxi, the first atomic bomb, nineteen sixty-four, hydrogen bomb, nineteen sixty-seven, and satellite Dongfanghong one, nineteen seventy, the Nanjing Yangtze River Bridge, nineteen sixty-eight, and Yuan Longping’s hybrid rice, nineteen seventy-three.
china/prc.c8f2da0ac668: Anshan Steel. Today: Anshan, Liaoning. In nineteen fifty-three three big new works at Anshan started producing — the beginning of New China’s steel industry.
china/prc.81617aa16c41: “Two bombs and one satellite”. Nineteen sixty-four, nineteen sixty-seven, nineteen seventy. Nuclear bombs, missiles and a man-made satellite. October nineteen sixty-four: China’s first atomic bomb was successfully tested. October nineteen sixty-six: China’s guided nuclear missile test succeeded. June nineteen sixty-seven: China’s first hydrogen bomb was successfully tested. April nineteen seventy: China launched its first man-made Earth satellite, Dongfanghong one, “The East Is Red one”. Scientists such as Deng Jiaxian and Qian Xuesen made outstanding contributions; their spirit is the “two bombs, one satellite” spirit.
china/prc.9f0fad25d083: Nineteen eighty, Special economic zones. Four special economic zones were set up: Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Shantou and Xiamen — “windows” for technology, management and knowledge. In nineteen eighty-eight Hainan became a province and the largest special economic zone.
china/prc.66373c624739: Nineteen eighty-four to two thousand one, All-round opening up. In nineteen eighty-four fourteen coastal port cities were opened; in nineteen ninety Shanghai Pudong was developed and opened; in two thousand one China joined the WTO. A pattern formed: special economic zones, coastal open cities, coastal open economic regions, inland.
china/prc.0c0240a2cecf: Hybrid rice. Nineteen seventy-three. Yuan Longping, “father of hybrid rice”. Nineteen seventy-three: Yuan Longping and his team bred indica hybrid rice for the first time in the world. Hybrid rice greatly raised rice yields and helped solve the problem of feeding China’s people. It has been grown in many countries, contributing to world food security.
china/prc.4c34388c4d99: Memory rhyme: Orbit, two thousand seven, far side, twenty nineteen, samples home, twenty twenty.
china/prc.7ff7c323e8a0: Common mix-up: The first special economic zones, nineteen eighty, were Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Shantou and Xiamen; Hainan became one in nineteen eighty-eight. Hong Kong returned on July first, nineteen ninety-seven, Macao on December twentieth, nineteen ninety-nine.
china/prc.3248efe1c9c4: October first, nineteen forty-nine, The founding ceremony. In September the CPPCC adopted the Common Programme and chose Beijing as the capital, the five-star red flag and the “March of the Volunteers”. On October first Mao Zedong proclaimed the founding of the People’s Republic of China at Tian’anmen.
china/prc.a1dcdab5173f: Memory rhyme: Tianhe, Wentian and Mengtian — equals a “T” in the sky, twenty twenty-two.
china/prc.aab8e685a9f1: Nineteen seventy-eight, A great turning point. The Third Plenary Session of the eleventh Central Committee, December nineteen seventy-eight, restored “emancipating the mind and seeking truth from facts”, shifted the focus to economic construction and launched reform and opening up. Farmers in Xiaogang Village, Anhui, began the household contract responsibility system.
china/prc.b184231b6251: Memory rhyme: two thousand three, Yang Liwei: China’s first step into space.
china/prc.fe7b7714a6af: Memory rhyme: two thousand eight Beijing-Tianjin; twenty seventeen Fuxing.
china/prc.67dfd5e9cedb: Yalu River. In October nineteen fifty the Chinese People’s Volunteers crossed the Yalu at Dandong to resist US aggression and aid Korea.
china/prc.25af0afec7db: Chang’e lunar programme. Two thousand seven, twenty nineteen. From orbiting the Moon to landing on its far side. Two thousand seven: Chang’e one, China’s first lunar probe, was launched. January twenty nineteen: Chang’e four made the first-ever soft landing on the far side of the Moon; the Yutu two rover explored it. Twenty twenty: Chang’e five brought lunar samples back to Earth.
china/prc.2faea0364333: Shenyang. Shenyang is a big industrial city. Its aircraft works built New China’s first jet fighter in nineteen fifty-six, and the Japanese invasion began here on September eighteenth, nineteen thirty-one.
china/prc.acd7d2cb9e6d: High-speed rail and Fuxing trains. Two thousand eight, twenty seventeen. The world’s largest high-speed rail network. Two thousand six: the Qinghai-Tibet Railway opened along its whole length. Two thousand eight: the Beijing-Tianjin intercity railway opened — China’s first high-speed line designed for three hundred fifty kilometers per hour. Twenty seventeen: the Fuxing, “Rejuvenation”, bullet trains, with independent intellectual property, entered service. China’s high-speed rail network is the longest in the world.

china/qin-han.ae3f522b0d57: In sixty B C E the Western Han set up the Protectorate of the Western Regions. From then on, the region of today’s Xinjiang came under the central government and became an inseparable part of China.
china/qin-han.cae70ba1ea39: In the late Warring States period Qin grew strong. From two hundred thirty to two hundred twenty-one B C E King Ying Zheng conquered Han, Zhao, Wei, Chu, Yan and Qi, founding the Qin dynasty — China’s first unified, multi-ethnic, centralized state — with its capital at Xianyang.
china/qin-han.96b3e228ffa5: Qin’s harsh rule provoked revolt. In two hundred nine B C E Chen Sheng and Wu Guang rose up at Dazexiang — the first large-scale peasant uprising in Chinese history. Qin fell in two hundred seven B C E; after the Chu-Han war, Liu Bang founded the Western Han in two hundred two B C E with its capital at Chang’an.
china/qin-han.bfb11c830b1b: The First Emperor ran the regions through commanderies and counties — thirty-six commanderies at first, later more than forty. Meng Tian drove back the Xiongnu and a wall was built from Lintao in the west to Liaodong in the east; in the south the Lingqu Canal joined the Xiang and Li rivers.
china/qin-han.0fa50fc9fcce: Under Emperor Wu, reigned one hundred forty-one to eighty-seven B C E, the Western Han reached its height. His generals Wei Qing and Huo Qubing drove back the Xiongnu and took the Hetao region and the Hexi Corridor, where four commanderies were set up: Wuwei, Zhangye, Jiuquan and Dunhuang.
china/qin-han.246a8d6c205e: To win the Yuezhi as allies against the Xiongnu, Emperor Wu sent Zhang Qian to the Western Regions in one hundred thirty-eight B C E; he went again in one hundred nineteen B C E. His journeys strengthened ties between the Central Plains and the Western Regions.
china/qin-han.e7b14b79e2c2: In twenty-five C E Liu Xiu founded the Eastern Han with its capital at Luoyang. Ban Chao restored Han control of the Western Regions and sent Gan Ying toward Daqin; Gan Ying reached the Persian Gulf. Cai Lun improved papermaking. Under Qin and Han the unified multi-ethnic state was built and consolidated.

china/reform-opening.b3464e823b3e: Ping An Finance Centre, twenty seventeen. About five hundred ninety-nine meters, one hundred eighteen floors — taller than One World Trade Center in New York, five hundred forty-one meters. From fishing villages to one of the world’s tallest towers in under forty years.
china/reform-opening.c9624ca40a76: Nineteen eighty: farms and fishing villages. August nineteen eighty: the Shenzhen Special Economic Zone was set up, just across a small river from Hong Kong. Why here? Hong Kong was already a rich trading city: money, factories and know-how could simply walk across the bridge. Slide back to nineteen eighty: almost nothing is taller than a tree.
china/reform-opening.c14fa520a31c: Diwang Building, nineteen ninety-six. About three hundred eighty-four meters — as tall as the Empire State Building’s roof, three hundred eighty-one meters. Finished in nineteen ninety-six, it was then the tallest building in China. By now Shenzhen made toys, clothes and electronics sold all over the world.
china/reform-opening.f34e3466b82e: Special economic zones. Nineteen eighty, nineteen eighty-eight. Nineteen eighty: four special economic zones, SEZs, were set up in Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Shantou and Xiamen — all on the coast of Guangdong and Fujian, near Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan. Inside a zone, special rules welcomed foreign companies, money and technology: a “window” to the world. Shenzhen grew fastest of all — people spoke of “Shenzhen speed”. Nineteen eighty-eight: Hainan, 海南, a tropical island about the size of Maryland, became a province and the largest SEZ.
china/reform-opening.535f990631dc: The Third Plenary Session of the eleventh Central Committee. December nineteen seventy-eight. Who met: the Communist Party’s Central Committee — a few hundred top leaders — in Beijing. Thinking: “free your mind, seek truth from facts”. Politics: stop putting “class struggle” first; shift the country’s main work to building the economy and start reform and opening up. Leadership: a new leading group formed with Deng Xiaoping, 邓小平, at its core. Why it matters: it opened the new period of reform, opening up and socialist modernisation.
china/reform-opening.dd295a2f93ca: Tianjin. Tianjin is Beijing’s gateway to the sea, on the Bohai. Since two thousand eight high-speed trains link the two cities in about thirty minutes.
china/reform-opening.40117a630847: Watch out: Shanghai and Guangzhou are open coastal cities, nineteen eighty-four, not special economic zones.
china/reform-opening.6a4f5035a4ee: Rural reform: the household contract responsibility system. from nineteen seventy-eight. Before: villagers farmed together in communes and shared the harvest about equally — work hard or not, you got the same. Nineteen seventy-eight: farmers in Xiaogang Village, 小岗村, Anhui, secretly divided the fields among families: each family would farm its own plot. The deal: “Hand in the state’s share, keep enough for the collective, and all the rest is ours.” The land still belongs to the collective; families contract it. Harvests jumped. The system spread nationwide, and village factories, township enterprises, sprang up.
china/reform-opening.07963d49bf33: Watch out: Families got the right to use and manage the land — not ownership. Compare: land reform, nineteen fifty, gave ownership to peasants.
china/reform-opening.8948de0519c0: Fourteen open coastal cities. Nineteen eighty-four. Nineteen eighty-four: after the zones proved a success, fourteen port cities were opened — a chain of harbours along the whole coast, from the cold north to the tropical south. North to south: Dalian, Qinhuangdao, Tianjin, Yantai, Qingdao, Lianyungang, Nantong, Shanghai, Ningbo, Wenzhou, Fuzhou, Guangzhou, Zhanjiang, Beihai. Zoom the map to the coast to see them all.
china/reform-opening.7fed0c19f660: Watch out: Two famous “turning points” — don’t swap them: Zunyi, nineteen thirty-five, saved the Party and the Red Army; this meeting, nineteen seventy-eight, began reform and opening up.
china/reform-opening.ffc3982249d6: The debate on the test of truth. May nineteen seventy-eight. After the “Cultural Revolution” ended in nineteen seventy-six, some leaders said: just keep doing whatever Mao decided, the “two whatevers”. May nineteen seventy-eight: a newspaper essay argued that an idea is true only if it works in real life — practice is the test. A nationwide debate followed. It freed people’s thinking and prepared minds for the great meeting of December nineteen seventy-eight.
china/reform-opening.3fb58294ac0a: Common mix-up: The order of opening is: special economic zones, nineteen eighty, open coastal cities, nineteen eighty-four, coastal open economic regions, nineteen eighty-five, inland. The first four zones were Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Shantou and Xiamen; Hainan came in nineteen eighty-eight, and Shanghai’s Pudong in nineteen ninety — Pudong is not a special economic zone.
china/reform-opening.721c3b199c41: Guomao Building, nineteen eighty-five. When finished in nineteen eighty-five it was the tallest building in China. Builders added one floor every three days — “Shenzhen speed” became a national saying. In nineteen ninety-two Deng Xiaoping looked out over the city from its revolving restaurant during his southern tour.
china/reform-opening.208621f39f95: K K one hundred, twenty eleven. About four hundred forty-two meters — the same height as Chicago’s Willis, Sears, Tower. By twenty eleven Shenzhen was home to technology companies known around the world.

china/revolution.815f7ea53ab9: Watch out: The Long March ended with the reunion of the three main forces in October nineteen thirty-six.
china/revolution.b64ad011c948: Battle of the Xiang River. Late November to early December nineteen thirty-four. The costliest battle of the early Long March. The Red Army broke through four enemy blockade lines; the last one lay along the Xiang River in northern Guangxi. It crossed the river at a very heavy price. Afterwards the Red Army turned toward Guizhou, where enemy forces were weaker, the Tongdao and Liping decisions.
china/revolution.64cc739cbaf4: Memory line: October nineteen thirty-five — Wuqi; October nineteen thirty-six — Huining.
china/revolution.2122f79ad07c: Nineteen forty-nine, Crossing the Yangtze. On April twenty-first, nineteen forty-nine, a million PLA troops crossed the river on a front from Jiangyin to Hukou. On April twenty-third they took Nanjing: the KMT’s reactionary rule collapsed. The New Democratic Revolution was won — the People’s Republic of China would be founded on October first, nineteen forty-nine.
china/revolution.8d2416f46aa2: Common mix-up: The September eighteenth Incident, nineteen thirty-one, began China’s partial resistance; the July seventh Incident, nineteen thirty-seven, began the nation-wide War of Resistance. The Central Red Army reached Wuqi in October nineteen thirty-five, but the Long March ended only when the three main forces met in October nineteen thirty-six.
china/revolution.9097ee80b569: Nineteen thirty-one to nineteen thirty-seven, Japan invades. On September eighteenth, nineteen thirty-one, Japan attacked Shenyang — the September eighteenth Incident began China’s partial resistance. On December twelfth, nineteen thirty-six, Zhang Xueliang and Yang Hucheng staged the Xi’an Incident; its peaceful settlement basically ended the civil war. On July seventh, nineteen thirty-seven, the Marco Polo Bridge Incident began the nation-wide War of Resistance.
china/revolution.c0e82f9e74c4: Nineteen forty-five to nineteen forty-seven, The War of Liberation begins. After the Chongqing negotiations, nineteen forty-five, the KMT attacked the Central Plains Liberated Area in June nineteen forty-six — full-scale civil war. In summer nineteen forty-seven the Liu-Deng army thrust into the Dabie Mountains, raising the curtain on the strategic counter-offensive.
china/revolution.75b64f21374e: Nineteen forty-eight to nineteen forty-nine, The three great campaigns. Liaoshen, Northeast, around Jinzhou; Huaihai, centred on Xuzhou; and Pingjin, Beiping-Tianjin — Beiping was liberated peacefully. They basically destroyed the main force of the KMT army.
china/revolution.6512453a3d1c: Nineteen twenty-one, The Communist Party of China is founded. In July nineteen twenty-one the First National Congress opened in Shanghai; on the last day it moved to a boat on South Lake, Jiaxing. An epoch-making event: the Chinese revolution took on a new look.
china/revolution.3463ece4ca12: Lugou, Marco Polo, Bridge. Today: southwest of Beijing. A stone bridge from eleven ninety-two with nearly five hundred carved lions. Japanese troops attacked here in nineteen thirty-seven, and all of China rose to resist.
china/revolution.7e86d2f2a24a: Dadu River and Luding Bridge. May nineteen thirty-five. Seizing the iron-chain bridge. May nineteen thirty-five: the Red Army forced a crossing of the Dadu River at Anshunchang. May twenty-ninth, nineteen thirty-five: twenty-two heroes climbed across the iron chains under fire and seized Luding Bridge. The main force crossed the Dadu River, avoiding the fate the enemy had planned for it.
china/revolution.71ce7ac71464: Crossing the Chishui River four times. January to March nineteen thirty-five. Escaping encirclement by surprise moves. Commanded by Mao Zedong, the Red Army crossed the Chishui River four times, back and forth. These swift, surprising moves confused the enemy and let the Red Army escape encirclement. The army then feinted toward Guiyang and Kunming and slipped west to the Jinsha River.
china/revolution.ba9833ddbec9: Ruijin. November nineteen thirty-one, October nineteen thirty-four. Red capital; the Long March begins. November nineteen thirty-one: the Provisional Central Government of the Chinese Soviet Republic was founded in Ruijin, Jiangxi, with Mao Zedong as chairman. The fifth counter-“encirclement” campaign failed because of the “Left” errors of Bo Gu, the Party’s leader at the time, and Otto Braun, Chinese name Li De, a military adviser sent from Moscow. October nineteen thirty-four: the main force of the Central Red Army was forced to leave the Central Revolutionary Base, from Ruijin, Yudu and other places, and began the Long March.
china/revolution.f897679f212c: Crossing the grasslands. August nineteen thirty-five. Marshes with no people and no food. August nineteen thirty-five: the Red Army crossed the marshy grasslands of northwest Sichuan, the Songpan grasslands. Many soldiers died from cold, hunger and the bogs. In September it broke through Lazikou, the gateway to Gansu.
china/revolution.3b95b889acff: Crossing the Jinsha River. Early May nineteen thirty-five. Jumping out of the encirclement. Early May nineteen thirty-five: the Red Army used a few small boats at Jiaopingdu to cross the Jinsha River, the upper Yangtze. It finally jumped out of the encirclement of several hundred thousand enemy troops.
china/revolution.29a0e6f2785c: Nineteen thirty-five to nineteen thirty-six, Victory of the Long March. Four crossings of the Chishui, across the Jinsha, the Dadu River and Luding Bridge, snow mountains and grasslands — in October nineteen thirty-five the Central Red Army reached Wuqi. In October nineteen thirty-six the three main forces met at Huining: the Long March ended in victory.
china/revolution.307ee09556ec: Memory line: Zunyi, nineteen thirty-five: turning danger into safety.
china/revolution.454004c670fd: Nineteen nineteen, The May Fourth Movement. At the Paris Peace Conference after World War One, Germany’s rights in Shandong Province were handed to Japan, not back to China. On May fourth students in Beijing rose up: “Fight for sovereignty abroad, punish traitors at home!” From June the centre moved to Shanghai and the working class became the main force.
china/revolution.9e37ee862af1: Nineteen twenty-four to nineteen twenty-seven, Cooperation and the Northern Expedition. The KMT, Nationalist Party, held its First Congress in Guangzhou in nineteen twenty-four and let Communists join: the first KMT-CPC cooperation. The Huangpu, Whampoa, Military Academy trained officers. In nineteen twenty-six the Northern Expedition marched north to overthrow the warlords — until Chiang Kai-shek’s nineteen twenty-seven coup in Shanghai broke the alliance.
china/revolution.c6a6c03e4d3d: Nineteen thirty-four to nineteen thirty-five, The Long March begins. After losing to the KMT’s fifth “encirclement” campaign, the Central Red Army left Ruijin in October nineteen thirty-four, broke four blockade lines at a terrible cost on the Xiang River, and turned to Guizhou. In January nineteen thirty-five the Zunyi Conference became a life-or-death turning point.
china/revolution.175f4980aef2: Jiajin Snow Mountain. June nineteen thirty-five. Climbing snow-capped peaks, meeting the Fourth Front Army. June nineteen thirty-five: in thin summer uniforms, the Red Army climbed the snow-covered Jiajin Mountain — more than four thousand meters, thirteen thousand feet, high, where the air is hard to breathe. It then met the Red Fourth Front Army at Maogong, Xiaojin, Sichuan.
china/revolution.a28f4e4d837b: Zunyi Conference. January nineteen thirty-five. A life-or-death turning point in Party history. January nineteen thirty-five, Zunyi, Guizhou: the Central Committee’s Politburo held an enlarged meeting. It concentrated on the decisive military and organisational questions, affirmed Mao Zedong’s correct military ideas and ended Bo Gu’s and Li De’s supreme military command. It in effect established Mao Zedong’s leading position in the Party Central Committee and the Red Army. It saved the Party, the Red Army and the Chinese revolution at an extremely critical moment, and marked the Party’s beginning to mature politically.
china/revolution.b9313af8b761: Watch out: Reaching Wuqi did not yet end the Long March as a whole — that came in October nineteen thirty-six.
china/revolution.56e4c97d6793: Nineteen thirty-seven to nineteen forty-five, The War of Resistance. Japan committed the Nanjing Massacre. Chinese forces fought back: Pingxingguan, nineteen thirty-seven, Taierzhuang, nineteen thirty-eight, the Hundred Regiments Offensive, nineteen forty. On August fifteenth, nineteen forty-five, Japan surrendered unconditionally; Taiwan returned to China. It was the first complete victory against foreign invasion in modern times.
china/revolution.9297e24d45f4: Nineteen twenty-seven, Armed struggle and Jinggangshan. On August first the Nanchang Uprising fired the first shot against the KMT reactionaries. The August seventh Meeting chose agrarian revolution and armed resistance. Mao Zedong led the Autumn Harvest Uprising troops to Jinggangshan — the first rural revolutionary base.
china/revolution.e9312e6a8d20: Huining reunion. October nineteen thirty-six. The three main Red Armies meet: the Long March ends. October nineteen thirty-six: the Red First, Second and Fourth Front Armies met at Huining, Gansu, and Jiangtaibao, Ningxia. The Long March ended in victory. Significance: it preserved and tempered the core forces of the revolution and moved the revolution’s headquarters to the northwest. The Long March spirit: fearing no hardship, never giving up, putting the people’s interests first.
china/revolution.9599d7e6071b: Wuqi Town, northern Shaanxi. October nineteen thirty-five. The Central Red Army reaches northern Shaanxi. October nineteen thirty-five: the Central Red Army reached Wuqi Town in northern Shaanxi and joined the Shaanxi Red Army. Northern Shaanxi became the base of the Chinese revolution.

china/seas-islands.bffdf9fa807e: Hainan Island. Hainan Province; tropical. About thirty-four thousand square kilometers — China’s second-largest island. Tropical all year: coconut palms, beaches and rubber trees. Sanya is on its southern tip. Hainan Province also governs the South China Sea Islands.
china/seas-islands.7f81d29f66df: South China Sea. China’s largest and deepest sea. About three point five million square kilometers — more than a third the size of the whole United States. Deep: about one thousand two hundred meters on average, over five thousand meters, sixteen thousand four hundred feet, at its deepest. Warm and tropical, full of coral reefs. The South China Sea Islands are coral islands. One of the world’s busiest shipping routes, with rich oil and gas.
china/seas-islands.6309b26bd7de: Yellow Sea. Between the mainland and the Korean Peninsula. Named for its yellowish water: rivers once carried huge loads of yellow silt into it. Average depth about forty-four meters, one hundred forty-four feet — still shallow. Big ports on its coast: Dalian and Qingdao. Off the Jiangsu coast there is a maze of sand ridges — a famous hazard for ships.
china/seas-islands.576e3e8d6e26: Xiamen Port. About twelve point six million TEU of containers in twenty twenty-three. That is roughly thirty-four thousand five hundred twenty-one twenty-foot containers every day. Compare all the ports in the bar chart in the Resources section.
china/seas-islands.c3a4f7953c83: Chongming Island. An alluvial island at the mouth of the Yangtze. Built by the river itself: mud and sand dropped by the Yangtze piled up into an island, an alluvial island, 冲积岛. About one thousand two hundred square kilometers — roughly the size of the city of Los Angeles — and still growing. Part of Shanghai.
china/seas-islands.003f18c26a8c: Tianjin Port. About twenty-two point two million TEU of containers in twenty twenty-three. That is roughly sixty thousand eight hundred twenty-two twenty-foot containers every day. Compare all the ports in the bar chart in the Resources section.
china/seas-islands.ef55ec156caa: Taiwan Island. China’s largest island; part of Taiwan Province. About thirty-six thousand square kilometers — a bit bigger than Maryland. Tall mountains run down its spine: Yushan, Jade Mountain, three thousand nine hundred fifty-two meters, is the highest peak in eastern China. Tropical in the south, subtropical in the north.
china/seas-islands.92758606611e: Don't mix up: Southernmost point equals Zengmu Ansha, about four degrees north, not Sanya, about eighteen degrees north.
china/seas-islands.40e245fea0d6: Shanghai Port. About forty-nine point two million TEU of containers in twenty twenty-three. That is roughly one hundred thirty-four thousand seven hundred ninety-five twenty-foot containers every day. Compare all the ports in the bar chart in the Resources section.
china/seas-islands.310a86736ad7: Zhongsha Islands. Mostly underwater banks and reefs. Most of the Zhongsha Islands are coral banks below the surface. Huangyan Island, 黄岩岛, is the part that rises above the sea.
china/seas-islands.f0dc71c47113: Ningbo-Zhoushan Port. About thirty-five point three million TEU of containers in twenty twenty-three. That is roughly ninety-six thousand seven hundred twelve twenty-foot containers every day. Compare all the ports in the bar chart in the Resources section.
china/seas-islands.3ad6ed84fe9b: Guangzhou Port. About twenty-five point four million TEU of containers in twenty twenty-three. That is roughly sixty-nine thousand five hundred eighty-nine twenty-foot containers every day. Compare all the ports in the bar chart in the Resources section.
china/seas-islands.08860070385b: Memory hook: Biggest islands: Taiwan one, Hainan two, Chongming three.
china/seas-islands.5990da8ea450: Bohai Sea. Almost surrounded by land. An inland sea, 内海: land wraps around it on three sides — Liaoning, Hebei, Tianjin and Shandong. Very shallow: about eighteen meters, sixty feet, deep on average — a six-storey building would stick out. About seventy-seven thousand square kilometers, a bit smaller than South Carolina. Its northern part freezes in winter. The Yellow River, Huang He, flows into it; its coast has China’s biggest offshore oilfield and the Changlu salt fields.
china/seas-islands.c885d80b1bce: Zengmu Ansha. About four degrees north, in the Nansha Islands. The southernmost point of China’s territory, at about four degrees north — farther south than Panama, about nine degrees north! “Ansha”, 暗沙, means a hidden sandbank: it lies about twenty meters under the sea. From Mohe in the far north, about fifty-three degrees north, to here is almost fifty degrees of latitude.
china/seas-islands.883450ed8dc2: Qiongzhou Strait. Between the Leizhou Peninsula and Hainan Island. Counts as an inland sea of China, like the Bohai. Only about twenty to forty kilometers, twelve to twenty-five miles, wide. Trains cross it on ferries: whole railway carriages roll onto ships.
china/seas-islands.d557b67766ee: Miaodao Islands. Today: Changdao, Yantai, Shandong. About thirty islands strung between Shandong and Liaodong.
china/seas-islands.83327ddeb637: Bohai Sea. Almost surrounded by Liaoning, Hebei, Tianjin and Shandong. It is shallow — only about eighteen meters deep on average — and parts freeze in winter.
china/seas-islands.f68f0e765cb8: Diaoyu Islands. Northeast of Taiwan Island, in the East China Sea. A small group of islands about one hundred seventy kilometers, one hundred five miles, northeast of Taiwan Island. Diaoyu Dao, the main island, is about four square kilometers — about the size of New York’s Central Park. China’s textbooks teach that the Diaoyu Islands are China’s inherent territory, attached to Taiwan Province, and standard Chinese maps always show them.
china/seas-islands.638e673687de: Xisha Islands. Southeast of Hainan Island. Coral islands with white sand and clear water. Yongxing Island here is the largest island of the South China Sea Islands and the seat of Sansha City, 三沙市, part of Hainan Province.
china/seas-islands.e0db0d799e06: Taiwan Strait. Between Fujian Province and Taiwan Island. China’s largest strait, linking the East China Sea and the South China Sea. About one hundred thirty kilometers, eighty miles, at its narrowest — a bit narrower than the Straits of Florida. Shallow: about sixty meters deep on average, with the even shallower Taiwan Banks in the south-west.
china/seas-islands.2b60bd3f9980: Qingdao Port. About twenty-eight point eight million TEU of containers in twenty twenty-three. That is roughly seventy-eight thousand nine hundred four twenty-foot containers every day. Compare all the ports in the bar chart in the Resources section.
china/seas-islands.9dfaa6bc3a69: Bohai Strait. Between the Liaodong and Shandong Peninsulas. The doorway between the Bohai and the Yellow Sea. About one hundred six kilometers, sixty-six miles, across at its narrowest. The Miaodao Islands, 庙岛群岛, sit across it like stepping stones.

china/silk-road-explorers.9bbd76e5a0d5: Zhang Qian. Western Han, one hundred thirty-eight to one hundred twenty-six B C. Emperor Wu of Han sent him to find the Yuezhi people and team up against the Xiongnu. Captured by the Xiongnu and held for more than ten years. Deserts and the high Pamir mountains. Captured again on the way home. First-hand knowledge of the Western Regions, 西域. News of Dayuan’s fine “heavenly horses”. Later: grapes, alfalfa, pomegranates, walnuts reach China. His journeys strengthened ties between the Central Plains and the Western Regions; the Silk Road took shape. In sixty B C the Western Han set up the Protectorate of the Western Regions — today’s Xinjiang formally came under the central government.
china/silk-road-explorers.ecdf0d1c66d9: Zheng He. Ming, fourteen oh five to fourteen thirty-three. The Yongle Emperor sent him to the “Western Oceans” to strengthen ties with overseas countries. Storms and typhoons at sea. Timing the monsoon winds right. Pirates near Palembang, 旧港. Finding the way across open ocean. A giraffe — welcomed as a “qilin”, 麒麟. Spices, gems and envoys from many lands. Took out: silk, porcelain, tea and iron goods. Seven voyages, fourteen oh five to fourteen thirty-three, reached more than thirty countries and regions in Asia and Africa — as far as the east coast of Africa and the Red Sea — decades before Europe’s great voyages.
china/silk-road-explorers.32bd1d379a68: Xuanzang. Tang, six twenty-nine to six forty-five, some say six twenty-seven. A young monk who wanted to study Buddhism where it began, in Tianzhu, 天竺, ancient India. Slipped out past Tang border guards, travel was banned. Lost his water in the Mohe-yan desert: four nights and five days without a drop. An icy pass over the Tian Shan. Thousands of kilometers of mountains on the way home. Six hundred fifty-seven Buddhist books, traditional figure. Translated over one thousand three hundred scrolls with his team. Great Tang Records on the Western Regions, “大唐西域记”. His book, Great Tang Records on the Western Regions, describes over one hundred lands. It is still a key source for the history of Central Asia and India.
china/silk-road-explorers.6fd1de1067a6: Jianzhen. Tang, seven forty-two to seven fifty-four. Japanese monks invited this famous teacher from Yangzhou to bring Buddhist rules to Japan. Attempt one: plans reported to officials — stopped. Attempts two to three: ships wrecked by storms. Attempt four: stopped by officials. Attempt five: blown fourteen days south to Hainan; he goes blind. Attempt six: success! Buddhist rules, precepts, for Japan. Tang architecture: Tōshōdai-ji temple, 唐招提寺. Medicine, calligraphy and sculpture. After six attempts and going blind, he reached Japan in seven fifty-four, some say seven fifty-three. He made an important contribution to cultural exchange between China and Japan.
china/silk-road-explorers.5b65fabc486b: Marco Polo. Yuan, twelve seventy-one to twelve ninety-five. A young merchant from Venice who travelled with his father and uncle to the court of Kublai Khan. Deserts and the high, cold Pamirs. A long illness on the way, about a year. A dangerous two-year sea voyage home. The Travels of Marco Polo, “马可, 波罗行纪”. Tales of Dadu, Beijing, paper money and post stations. Europe’s curiosity about the East. His book describes the wealth of Yuan China and the splendour of Dadu, and made many Europeans eager to reach the East. Some scholars doubt parts of his story.

china/song-yuan.0b5dee59e918: Stern rudder. Steers the ship. A large rudder hung at the stern steers the ship. A pottery boat model of the Eastern Han found in Guangzhou already has a stern rudder, one of the earliest in the world. Rudder at the back, compass on deck: steering and direction.
china/song-yuan.89d011ea468d: Huining, Jin capital. Today: Acheng, Harbin, Heilongjiang. Wanyan Aguda of the Jurchen founded the Jin here; within twelve years the Jin destroyed both the Liao and the Northern Song.
china/song-yuan.339741f00135: Quanzhou harbour, Quanzhou equals chwen-joe. A world-famous port of the Song and Yuan. Quanzhou is on China’s southeast coast, about as far south as Miami. In the Song, overseas trade exceeded earlier dynasties; Guangzhou and Quanzhou were great ports known around the world. Quanzhou was a starting point of the Maritime Silk Road; merchants from Arabia, Persia and Southeast Asia came to trade. In twenty twenty-one “Quanzhou: Emporium of the World in Song-Yuan China” joined the UNESCO World Heritage List. Song-Yuan sea trade: remember “Guang-Quan”, Guangzhou and Quanzhou.
china/song-yuan.7985d63c1bc7: Xingqing, Western Xia capital. Today: Yinchuan, Ningxia. Li Yuanhao declared himself emperor here in ten thirty-eight. The great royal tombs of the Western Xia stand west of the city.
china/song-yuan.23a7490cd45e: The Jurchen Jin, eleven fifteen, destroyed the Liao, eleven twenty-five, and then the Northern Song, eleven twenty-seven, the Jingkang Incident. Zhao Gou founded the Southern Song, later based in Lin’an. After peace talks the border ran along the Huai River — Dasan Pass.
china/song-yuan.6c9515ee9692: Yingxian Wooden Pagoda. Today: Ying County, Shanxi. About sixty-seven meters tall and made entirely of wood without nails, it has stood for over nine hundred fifty years and survived earthquakes.
china/song-yuan.ecbfc998939f: In twelve oh six Temüjin united the Mongol tribes and was honoured as Genghis Khan. In twelve seventy-one Kublai named his state Yuan and the next year made Dadu, today’s Beijing, the capital. In twelve seventy-six Yuan troops took Lin’an, and in twelve seventy-nine the Yuan unified the whole country.
china/song-yuan.ea27e5661e1d: The Yuan created the province system: the Central Secretariat ran the “heartland” around Dadu, and provinces, 行省, ran the rest. The Xuanzheng Yuan governed Tibet, and the Penghu Inspectorate governed Penghu and Liuqiu, Taiwan. Today’s provinces grew out of this system.
china/song-yuan.132a36990776: Song ocean-going ship. Big, strong and built for the open sea. Song shipbuilding led the world: ships were large, carried heavy loads and resisted storms. A Song ship found in Quanzhou Bay in nineteen seventy-four had a hull divided into thirteen compartments. What survives is about twenty-four meters, seventy-nine feet, long, the length of a tennis court. Big ships could carry hundreds of people and sailed to Southeast Asia, South Asia, Arabia and East Africa, a sea voyage of more than six thousand miles, ten thousand kilometers. Three “big” things about Song ships: big hull, big load, big voyages.
china/song-yuan.f2ab3d4dd439: Song times: the Northern Song, nine sixty, stood beside the Liao, Khitan, and the Western Xia, Tangut. In ten oh five the Song and Liao made the Chanyuan Treaty: the Song paid silver and silk each year, and a long peace followed.
china/song-yuan.b1756567cb05: Maritime Trade Office, Shibosi, shir-bwo-suh. The government office that managed sea trade. The Song government set up Maritime Trade Offices in Guangzhou, Quanzhou, Mingzhou and other ports to manage overseas trade. They inspected ships, collected taxes and bought goods for the state. In the Southern Song, income from sea trade became an important source of government revenue. Shi-bo equals “market and ships”: like an ancient customs house.
china/song-yuan.faa4acff424e: Watertight compartments. If one compartment leaks, the ship stays afloat. Thick wooden bulkheads split the hull into separate, sealed compartments. If one compartment is holed and floods, water cannot spread to the others, so the ship can keep sailing. The bulkheads also brace the hull and make it stronger. The watertight-bulkhead technology of Chinese junks was inscribed by UNESCO in twenty ten as intangible cultural heritage in need of urgent safeguarding. Try the Flooding test!

china/spring-warring.933b1d38aa15: From two hundred thirty to two hundred twenty-one B C E King Ying Zheng of Qin conquered the six states one by one — Han, Zhao, Wei, Chu, Yan, Qi — and in two hundred twenty-one B C E unified China. You will meet the Qin dynasty in the next unit.
china/spring-warring.672b3dc40487: In seven hundred seventy B C E King Ping moved east to Luoyi and the Eastern Zhou began. It has two parts: the Spring and Autumn period, seven hundred seventy to four hundred seventy-six B C E, and the Warring States period, four hundred seventy-five to two hundred twenty-one B C E.
china/spring-warring.df6a5c6ebc53: In three hundred fifty-six B C E Duke Xiao of Qin backed Shang Yang’s reforms: private land could be bought and sold; farming and fighting were rewarded; ranks were given for military merit; counties were set up and run by officials sent by the ruler. Qin became the richest and strongest state of the late Warring States.
